articles.title: Spain deploys military after thousands of Moroccan migrants cross border illegally; 9 killed
articles.description: Spain deployed its military to Ceuta after thousands of migrants crossed from Morocco.  The sudden influx overwhelmed security forces, leading to a severe border crisis.  Authorities confirmed an agreement with Morocco for the return of illegal migrants.  The reason for the surge remains unclear, with various factors suggested.  Ceuta, a Spanish enclave, is a key point for migration into Europe.

articles.title: Meta India head, social media users booked over PM Modi posts
articles.description: Cybercrime police registered cases against social media account operators and Meta India's head.  These cases involve morphed and objectionable content targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  BJP supporters filed complaints alleging manipulated videos and images were circulated online.  Police are tracing the operators behind the social media accounts involved.  Notices have been issued to Meta regarding the reported objectionable links.

articles.title: 5 killed in Bhiwandi building collapse; several feared trapped
articles.description: A residential building collapsed in Bhiwandi, killing at least five people. Several individuals are feared trapped inside the debris after the structure fell. Rescue teams are actively searching the collapsed building using heavy machinery. The building had been declared dangerous and notices were issued for evacuation. Most families had moved out, but some occupants remained inside.

articles.title: Who is Seema Kaliramna? The mother and PhD scholar who won CWG bronze
articles.description: Seema Kaliramna secured a bronze medal in the women's discus throw at the Commonwealth Games 2026. She achieved a best throw of 58.65 meters, earning India another medal. Kaliramna made an inspiring comeback after motherhood and pursuing her PhD studies. Her husband and coach, Ravinder Kaliramna, played a significant role in her success. She dedicated her medal to her husband's unwavering support and sacrifices.

articles.title: 10 climbers, including Nirmal Purja, missing after avalanche on Broad Peak in PoK's Gilgit-Baltistan
articles.description: Ten international climbers, including renowned Nepal-born mountaineer Nirmal Purja are missing after an avalanche struck Broad Peak. A tracking device shows Purja's location has shifted, offering a small hope for rescuers. Poor weather has so far prevented helicopters from taking off, delaying aerial search-and-rescue operations. Authorities were preparing to deploy helicopters on Friday morning if weather conditions improved.

articles.title: Russian strikes across Ukraine kill 10; missiles hit Poland too
articles.description: Russian missile and drone attacks killed at least ten civilians, including children, and injured over fifty. Nato scrambled warplanes after a Russian missile briefly crossed into Poland's western airspace. Ukrainian President Zelensky stated North Korean missiles were used in the attack on Thursday. Russia targeted Ukrainian air bases and arms factories, while Ukraine attacked Russia's oil sector.

articles.title: xAI sues US state over law banning 'nudification' tech
articles.description: Elon Musk's xAI company has sued Minnesota over its new law. This law bans AI nudification technology on websites and applications. The lawsuit challenges the state's authority to regulate AI-generated content. xAI argues the law is too broad and unconstitutional. The case could set a precedent for AI regulation by states.

articles.title: Formal retail credit access doubles over past decade
articles.description: Formal retail credit penetration in India more than doubled over the past decade. Consumption-led lending, including personal loans, drove this significant growth. Credit access expanded to younger borrowers and women across India. Northern and central states saw increased credit activity, while western and southern regions moderated. This shift reflects credit being used for lifestyle rather than asset acquisition.

articles.title: After surviving Hurricane Irma, this 16-year-old created a programme that teaches students what schools didn't
articles.description: After surviving Hurricane Irma as a child, 16-year-old Elise Raurell turned her experience into action by creating Storm Smart, a student-led hurricane preparedness programme. Developed as her Girl Scout Gold Award project, the initiative teaches children how to prepare for, stay safe during and recover after hurricanes through peer-to-peer learning. Having already reached nearly 500 students, Storm Smart aims to fill a critical gap in school education while empowering young people to protect themselves and their communities.
